title: P99/P95 tail latency deep dive - Aurora Systems
next_steps: Send consolidated benchmark spreadsheet and runtime tuning guide
Schedule on-prem benchmark run (Aurora infra) next week
Share SOC2 and network architecture docs; confirm IP allowlist details
action_items: Jordan Reyes: Share consolidated benchmark spreadsheet and pricing estimate (due 2026-04-02)
Priya Malhotra: Create recommended batching/KV cache config and run simulator against Aurora traces (due 2026-04-06)
Maya Chen: Provide current p95/p99 traces and representative request distributions (due 2026-03-31)
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Reyes: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. 00:07 Eli Navarro: thanks Jordan, excited to dig in; we've been seeing some p99 spikes hitting our product floor. 00:12 Priya Malhotra: hey all, Priya from Redwood infra team, I'll drive the technical part. 00:16 Maya Chen: quick context: we're running a hybrid setup, some hosted models for burst and on-prem for sensitive data behind our VPC. 00:24 Jordan Reyes: perfect, goal for today - p95/p99 deep dive across streaming vs non-streaming, KV cache behavior, batching, and network hops that might be adding tail latency. 00:34 Samir Patel: we typically see p95 ~120ms but p99 jumps to 900ms on large prompts, esp during traffic bursts. 00:41 Priya Malhotra: ok that's useful; can you describe the request distribution? like token lengths, streaming usage, and concurrency. 00:48 Maya Chen: 70% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 20% mid (64-512), 10% long documents; streaming enabled for chat paths. concurrency avg 120, burst to 600. 00:58 Priya Malhotra: thanks - that pattern can surface both runtime scheduling stalls and network queuing. two main buckets: model-side compute tail (kv cache misses, attention compute) and infra/networking (GRPC timeouts, multi-hop through NAT/GW). 01:12 Diego Alvarez: one note - are you using warmed KV cache across requests? i.e., same session or shared prefixes. 01:18 Maya Chen: we try to reuse sessions for chat, but many requests are cold because we spin ephemeral containers for privacy-sensitive flows. 01:25 Priya Malhotra: that explains some p99s - cold KV cache causes extra decoding overhead since KV cache needs to be rebuilt; also cold process start if on-prem autoscaler is spinning nodes. 01:33 Eli Navarro: curious about streaming vs non-streaming - sometimes our UI shows first-token latency fine but final completion much later. 01:40 Priya Malhotra: streaming hides latency for first byte; p95 often improves, p99 sometimes worse because of tail chunking and small-chunk backpressure - network Nagle-ish effects and head-of-line blocking can amplify tail. 01:52 Samir Patel: so for streaming we get better perceived latency but tail may still be bad - how do we measure properly? 01:58 Priya Malhotra: measure both first-byte and full-completion latencies, and instrument per-hop timing: ingest -> routing -> model runtime (token loop) -> network egress. Redwood tracing SDK can break that down; we'll share an instrumented span map. 02:12 Jordan Reyes: also look at request size quantiles and batching windows - we often see long tails when the runtime waits to fill batch vs strict latency SLO. 02:20 Maya Chen: what are batching knobs we can tune? 02:23 Priya Malhotra: two levers - max_batch_size and batching_timeout_ms. increase batch size for throughput but may hurt 95th; reduce timeout for latency but reduce GPU utilization. We also recommend dynamic batching profiles by route: set aggressive batching for background scoring and conservative for interactive chat. 02:38 Diego Alvarez: kv cache policy matters too - prefix dedup and TTL, plus whether you pin KV across sessions. on-prem we can pin long-lived LRU caches to reduce rebuilds. 02:48 Eli Navarro: quantization - can that affect tail? we're using int8 models for cost. 02:52 Priya Malhotra: yes, quantization affects throughput/latency tradeoffs; INT8 often improves throughput but can increase jitter if kernels are suboptimal on certain hardware or if fallback to slower kernels occurs for some ops. we recommend profiling top operators and using Redwood's kernel-selection flags; we'll share a kernel mismatch report. 03:09 Samir Patel: network hops - we have a NAT, a proxy, and then the Redwood Private router; any guidance? 03:15 Priya Malhotra: each hop adds tail risk: NAT connection churn, proxy buffering, TLS handshake retries. for private deployments we recommend keeping routing plane inside VPC, using keepalive settings, and increasing socket pool sizes on the proxy. also consider colocating model endpoints in the same AZ. 03:32 Maya Chen: we'd love concrete numbers - what does Redwood see p99 contributions from runtime vs network? 03:38 Priya Malhotra: typical breakdown on similar workloads: runtime token loop 60% of p99 mass, scheduling/queueing 20%, network/hops 20% - but cold starts can flip that. in our customers who pinned instances and used KV pinning, runtime p99 dropped by ~3-4x. 03:54 Eli Navarro: do you have a recommended rollout for on-prem vs hosted? we want initial hosted to move fast but need privacy for some flows. 04:02 Jordan Reyes: common pattern - start with hosted for baseline, run controlled benchmarks, then move sensitive traffic to Private deployment with identical config; use traffic routing policies and gradual canary. 04:12 Priya Malhotra: for benchmarking, provide representative traces; we'll run replayed requests with both streaming and non-streaming modes, measure first-byte and end-to-end, and produce a p95/p99 waterfall. 04:22 Maya Chen: what about autoscaling spikes? we saw long tail during scale-up. 04:26 Priya Malhotra: scale-up can cause cold processes that require model warm-up; use a combination of burst-capacity pools and pre-warming hooks. Dedicated or Private deployments can reserve GPU pools that avoid cold start. 04:36 Diego Alvarez: quantization profiling - sometimes INT8 fallback happens only on rare operator shapes leading to infrequent slow paths; we run operator heatmaps to catch that. 04:45 Samir Patel: are there config templates we can start with? 04:48 Priya Malhotra: yes - we'll share a recommended config: batching timeout 5ms for interactive, 50-100ms for scoring; max_batch_size 8-64 depending on model; keep KV cache pinned for chat flows; socket keepalive 30s, reuse connections. link: https://redwood.ai/configs/latency-playbook (note: placeholder). 05:05 Eli Navarro: regarding observability, can we see token-level timing? 05:09 Diego Alvarez: Redwood tracing includes per-token loop durations aggregated into histograms; you can export spans to your tracing backend. 05:16 Maya Chen: security concerns - we need SOC2 docs and network diagrams before Private trial. 05:20 Jordan Reyes: we'll send SOC2 + network architecture and IP allowlist; Priya can share the NV benchmark script. 05:26 Priya Malhotra: quick demo of a small synthetic run - (Priya screen-shares, audio only) we replayed 10k requests with Aurora trace; baseline hosted p99 = 780ms, after KV pinning and sizing batch windows we got p99 = 220ms; streaming first-byte p50 = 38ms. 05:46 Samir Patel: wow that gap is promising. 05:49 Eli Navarro: what's the expected delta on cost when we pin more cache and reserve GPUs? 05:53 Jordan Reyes: tradeoff is reserved capacity cost vs reduced tail latency and better SLOs; we'll include cost delta in the benchmark spreadsheet. 05:59 Maya Chen: any risks with quantization on safety/regressions? 06:03 Priya Malhotra: yes, quantization can degrade quality for some models - we recommend running quality evals with your prompts and compare embeddings/regression alerts via Redwood Optimize. 06:12 Jordan Reyes: recap - Redwood to run replay benchmarks, share configs/docs, Aurora to provide traces and network details, schedule on-prem run next week. 06:20 Eli Navarro: agreed - thanks team. 06:22 Jordan Reyes: action items, I'll send the spreadsheet and SOC2; Priya will produce batching/KV recommendations; Maya to upload traces. 06:30 Maya Chen: uploading right after this call, thanks. 06:33 Jordan Reyes: cool, we'll sync next Tuesday for results review. 06:36 End of recording
